item.title: CSS Variables
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In a real stylesheet, the same brand colour may appear fifty times. Changing it means fifty edits. CSS variables (officially "custom properties") let you store a value once and reuse it everywhere. They also make dark mode and themes easy.

Defining and using a variable

<style>
  :root {
    --brand: #2563eb;
    --radius: 10px;
  }
  .btn {
    background: var(--brand);
    color: white;
    border: none;
    padding: 10px 20px;
    border-radius: var(--radius);
  }
  .link { color: var(--brand); }
  .box { border: 2px solid var(--brand); border-radius: var(--radius); padding: 12px; margin-top: 12px; }
</style>
<button class="btn">Button</button>
<a class="link" href="#">A link</a>
<div class="box">A box</div>
  • A variable name starts with two hyphens: --brand.
  • :root means the <html> element, so variables defined there are available everywhere.
  • var(--brand) uses the value.

Now change --brand to #16a34a and everything turns green at once.

Fallback values

.title { color: var(--heading-color, #111827); }

If --heading-color isn't defined, the fallback after the comma is used.

Variables are inherited and can be overridden

A variable can be redefined on any element, and the new value applies to that element and its children:

<style>
  :root { --accent: #2563eb; }
  .card { border-top: 4px solid var(--accent); padding: 12px; margin-bottom: 10px; background: #f8fafc; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
  .card h3 { color: var(--accent); margin: 0; }
  .card.success { --accent: #16a34a; }
  .card.danger  { --accent: #dc2626; }
</style>
<div class="card"><h3>Default</h3></div>
<div class="card success"><h3>Success</h3></div>
<div class="card danger"><h3>Danger</h3></div>

One set of card styles, three colour variants, each changing just one variable. This is how design systems build components.

A dark mode in a few lines

<style>
  :root {
    --bg: #ffffff;
    --text: #1f2937;
    --muted: #6b7280;
    --surface: #f3f4f6;
    --brand: #2563eb;
  }
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    :root {
      --bg: #0f172a;
      --text: #e5e7eb;
      --muted: #94a3b8;
      --surface: #1e293b;
      --brand: #60a5fa;
    }
  }
  body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 20px; }
  .panel { background: var(--surface); padding: 16px; border-radius: 10px; }
  .panel p { color: var(--muted); }
  a { color: var(--brand); }
</style>
<div class="panel">
  <h3>Automatic dark mode</h3>
  <p>Switch your system to dark mode and this page follows.</p>
  <a href="#">A link</a>
</div>

The components only use variables. Dark mode simply swaps the variable values. VitalStack's own dark mode works this way, with a toggle button that sets a data-theme attribute on <html>:

:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg: #0f172a;
  --text: #e5e7eb;
}

Design tokens: organising variables

Large projects group their variables by purpose. These are often called design tokens:

:root {
  /* Colours */
  --color-brand: #2563eb;
  --color-text: #1f2937;
  --color-muted: #6b7280;
  --color-border: #e5e7eb;

  /* Spacing scale */
  --space-1: 0.25rem;
  --space-2: 0.5rem;
  --space-3: 1rem;
  --space-4: 1.5rem;
  --space-5: 2rem;

  /* Typography */
  --font-body: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-code: "Source Code Pro", monospace;
  --text-sm: 0.875rem;
  --text-lg: 1.25rem;

  /* Shapes */
  --radius-sm: 6px;
  --radius-lg: 14px;
  --shadow: 0 4px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08);
}

Using a fixed scale (--space-3 instead of random values like 13px, 17px, 22px) makes a design look consistent.

Calculating with variables

:root { --gap: 16px; }
.section { padding: calc(var(--gap) * 2); }
.tight { margin-top: calc(var(--gap) / 2); }

calc() combines variables with maths, even mixing units: calc(100% - var(--sidebar-width)).

Changing variables with JavaScript

<style>
  :root { --hue: 220; }
  .swatch { height: 80px; border-radius: 8px; background: hsl(var(--hue) 80% 55%); }
</style>
<div class="swatch"></div>
<label>Hue <input type="range" min="0" max="360" value="220" id="hue"></label>
<script>
  document.getElementById("hue").addEventListener("input", function () {
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--hue", this.value);
  });
</script>

Drag the slider and the colour updates live. Variables are the bridge between JavaScript and CSS.

Common mistakes

  • One hyphen instead of two: -brand isn't a variable.
  • **Forgetting var()**: color: --brand; does nothing.
  • Spaces or typos in names; variable names are case-sensitive.
  • Defining variables inside one component and expecting them to work in others. Put shared ones in :root.

Exercise

  1. Move your profile page's colours, radius and spacing into :root variables.
  2. Add a dark mode with prefers-color-scheme by redefining only the variables.
  3. Make "success", "warning" and "danger" versions of a message box by changing one variable each.
  4. Add a range slider that changes a variable with JavaScript.

Summary

  • Define variables with --name: value (usually on :root) and use them with var(--name).
  • Variables inherit and can be overridden per element, which makes component variants easy.
  • Dark mode = swap variable values.
  • Design tokens (colours, spacing, fonts) keep a whole site consistent.

Next, you'll use the whole CSS course to style your profile page project.
item.excerpt:encoded: Store colours, spacing and fonts in custom properties, use var() with fallbacks, build a dark mode, and organise a stylesheet around design tokens.

item.title: CSS Project: Style Your Profile Page
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
At the end of the HTML course you built a complete profile page. Now you'll make it look professional using everything from this course: variables, the box model, Flexbox, Grid, responsive design and transitions. Work through the steps in order, testing as you go.

Step 0: Start with your HTML

Use your page from the HTML project. If you don't have it, this short version is enough to follow along:

<header class="site-header">
  <div class="container header-inner">
    <a class="logo" href="#">Asha Verma</a>
    <nav aria-label="Main">
      <ul class="nav">
        <li><a href="#about">About</a></li>
        <li><a href="#skills">Skills</a></li>
        <li><a href="#projects">Projects</a></li>
        <li><a href="#contact">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </div>
</header>
<main class="container">
  <section id="about" class="hero">
    <img class="avatar" src="https://picsum.photos/id/64/240/240" alt="Asha smiling at a desk" width="240" height="240">
    <div>
      <h1>Hi, I'm Asha</h1>
      <p class="lead">Beginner web developer building one small project every week.</p>
      <a class="btn" href="#contact">Get in touch</a>
    </div>
  </section>
  <section id="projects">
    <h2>Projects</h2>
    <div class="cards">
      <article class="card"><h3>Recipe page</h3><p>Headings, lists and images.</p></article>
      <article class="card"><h3>Timetable</h3><p>Tables with merged cells.</p></article>
      <article class="card"><h3>Profile page</h3><p>Everything together, now with CSS.</p></article>
    </div>
  </section>
</main>
<footer class="site-footer"><div class="container"><small>© Asha Verma</small></div></footer>

The only change from plain HTML: a few classes added as styling hooks.

Step 1: Variables and a reset

Put this at the top of your stylesheet (or a <style> element while testing):

:root {
  --bg: #f8fafc;
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --text: #1f2937;
  --muted: #64748b;
  --border: #e2e8f0;
  --brand: #2563eb;
  --brand-dark: #1e40af;
  --radius: 14px;
  --shadow: 0 4px 14px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.08);
  --font: "Inter", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
}

*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--text);
  font-family: var(--font);
  line-height: 1.6;
}

img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }

Step 2: A centred container

.container {
  max-width: 1000px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 20px;
}

Every section now lines up on the same centred column.

Step 3: Header with Flexbox

.site-header {
  background: var(--surface);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: 10;
}
.header-inner {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 12px;
  padding-block: 14px;
}
.logo {
  font-weight: 800;
  font-size: 1.25rem;
  color: var(--text);
  text-decoration: none;
}
.nav {
  display: flex;
  gap: 4px;
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}
.nav a {
  display: block;
  padding: 8px 12px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  color: var(--muted);
  text-decoration: none;
  transition: background-color 0.2s, color 0.2s;
}
.nav a:hover {
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--brand);
}

(padding-block sets top and bottom padding together.)

Step 4: The hero section

.hero {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  text-align: center;
  gap: 24px;
  padding: 48px 0;
}
.avatar {
  width: 160px;
  height: 160px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  object-fit: cover;
  border: 4px solid var(--surface);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
.hero h1 {
  font-size: clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3rem);
  line-height: 1.15;
  margin: 0 0 8px;
}
.lead {
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  color: var(--muted);
  max-width: 45ch;
  margin: 0 auto 20px;
}
@media (min-width: 700px) {
  .hero {
    flex-direction: row;
    text-align: left;
  }
  .lead { margin-left: 0; }
}

Mobile-first: stacked and centred on phones, photo beside text from 700px.

Step 5: Buttons

.btn {
  display: inline-block;
  background: var(--brand);
  color: white;
  padding: 12px 24px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  font-weight: 600;
  text-decoration: none;
  transition: background-color 0.2s, transform 0.2s;
}
.btn:hover {
  background: var(--brand-dark);
  transform: translateY(-2px);
}
.btn:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #f59e0b;
  outline-offset: 3px;
}

Step 6: Responsive project cards with Grid

.cards {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr));
  gap: 20px;
}
.card {
  background: var(--surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  padding: 20px;
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
  transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s;
}
.card:hover {
  transform: translateY(-4px);
  box-shadow: 0 12px 24px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.12);
}
.card h3 { margin-top: 0; }
.card p { color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 0; }

Step 7: Footer, forms and tables

.site-footer {
  margin-top: 64px;
  padding: 24px 0;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--border);
  color: var(--muted);
  text-align: center;
}

input, textarea {
  width: 100%;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 8px;
  font: inherit;
  background: var(--surface);
  color: var(--text);
}
input:focus, textarea:focus {
  outline: none;
  border-color: var(--brand);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(37 99 235 / 0.25);
}

table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; }
th, td { padding: 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); text-align: left; }
tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: var(--bg); }

font: inherit makes form fields use the page font instead of the browser's default. border-collapse: collapse merges table borders into single lines. The focus style replaces the outline with an equally visible ring, so keyboard users can still see where they are.

Step 8: Dark mode

Because everything uses variables, dark mode is one block:

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --bg: #0b1120;
    --surface: #111827;
    --text: #e5e7eb;
    --muted: #94a3b8;
    --border: #1f2937;
    --brand: #60a5fa;
    --brand-dark: #3b82f6;
  }
}

Step 9: Final checks

  • ☐ Test at 320px, 768px and 1280px wide: no horizontal scrolling.
  • ☐ Tab through the page: every link and button shows focus.
  • ☐ Check text contrast in both light and dark mode.
  • ☐ Turn on "reduce motion" and add the reduced-motion block from the transitions lesson.
  • ☐ Validate the CSS at jigsaw.w3.org/css-validator.

Ideas to go further

  • Add a skills section as a row of pill-shaped tags with flex-wrap.
  • Add a theme toggle button (you'll be able to write the JavaScript after the first few JavaScript lessons).
  • Publish it for free on GitHub Pages or Netlify and share the link.

Summary

  • Variables and a small reset give a consistent foundation.
  • Flexbox handles the header and hero; Grid handles the card layout.
  • Mobile-first media queries and clamp() make it responsive.
  • Variables make dark mode a single block of CSS.

You've finished the CSS course. Next comes JavaScript, where you'll make your pages interactive.
